examples.trans: Kostya, are we going home right now or what?

examples.text: Ты поезжай домой, а я останусь здесь.
examples.trans: You go on home, and I will stay here.

examples.text: Помни, что я жду тебя дома.
examples.trans: Remember that I am waiting for you at home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'worry'.

examples.text: Не волнуйся.
examples.trans: Don't worry.

examples.text: Я волнуюсь.
examples.trans: I'm nervous.

examples.text: Не волнуйся, не буду.
examples.trans: Don't worry, I won't.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'in the morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Не волнуйся, утром сразу приеду домой.
examples.trans: Do not worry, in the morning I will come straight home.

examples.text: Доброе утро!
examples.trans: Good morning!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро!
examples.trans: What a lovely morning!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.text: Не волнуйся, утром сразу приеду домой.
examples.trans: Do not worry, in the morning I will come straight home.

examples.text: Сразу видно.
examples.trans: You can see it at once.

examples.text: Я сразу понял.
examples.trans: I understood at once.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will arrive', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.text: Ты на какой машине приехала?
examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: Паша приехал.
examples.trans: Pasha has arrived.

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?
